data.long_meaning: Elisaveta is derived from the Hebrew name Elisheba, meaning 'My God is an oath' or 'God's oath'. In the Bible, Elisheba is the wife of Aaron, the brother of Moses. This name is also associated with Saint Elisabeth of Hungary, a 13th-century Christian saint. The name Elisaveta carries the meaning “God's oath of salvation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Elisaveta usually hope their child will grow to embody god's oath of salvation and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Elisaveta
in_latin.long_meaning: Elisaveta est nomen virginis Israhae, quae habitavit sub lege Moysi, et fuit sancta coram Deo, quia credebat verbum Dei et non contempsit se propter fidem suam. Elisaveta est exemplum fidei et obedientiae, et in Evangelio Joannis est narratio de sua conceptione in utero, quae fuit miraculum Dei et signum gratiae suae. Nomen Elisaveta significat 'Deus exaltavit' et est nomen sanctum in Ecclesia Catholica Romana, quae celebrat dies natalis Elisavetae die 21 Novembris.

in_english.long_meaning: Elisaveta is the name of a virgin of Israel, who lived under the law of Moses and was considered holy before God, as she believed in God's word and did not despise herself because of her faith. Elisaveta is an example of faith and obedience, and in the Gospel of John, there is a narrative of her conception in the womb, which was a miracle of God and a sign of His grace. The name Elisaveta means 'God has exalted' and is a holy name in the Roman Catholic Church, which celebrates Elisaveta's birthday on November 21st.
